title: Closed base change preserves completed Jacobian torsion
statement: Let $A$ be a commutative Noetherian ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], $I\subseteq A$ an ideal, and $P=\widehat{A[x_1,\ldots,x_r]}_I$ for $r\geq0$ [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring, def-weil-pbc-adic-completion]. Let $J\subseteq P$ be an ideal and put $E=P/J$, assumed $I$-adically complete. Suppose some $c\geq0$ satisfies $I^c\ker\delta=I^c\operatorname{coker}\delta=0$, where $\delta:J/J^2\to E^{\oplus r}$ sends $f\bmod J^2$ to $(\partial f/\partial x_i\bmod J)_i$, using continuous polynomial derivatives. Let $H\subseteq A$ be any ideal, put $A_0=A/H$, and let $K\subseteq A_0$ be an ideal with $V(IA_0)=V(K)$ in $\operatorname{Spec}A_0$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. Then $E_0=E/HE$ is $K$-adically complete and admits an $A_0$-algebra presentation $E_0\cong\widehat{A_0[y_1,\ldots,y_s]}_K/J_0$ for some finite $s\geq0$ and ideal $J_0$. For this presentation there is an integer $d\geq0$ such that $K^d$ annihilates both kernel and cokernel of the continuous conormal differential $J_0/J_0^2\to E_0^{\oplus s}$, $f\mapsto(\partial f/\partial y_j)_j$.

proof.text: Put $R=A[x_1,\ldots,x_r]$ and $R_0=A_0[x_1,\ldots,x_r]$. The finite-type Noetherian permanence theorem applied to $A\to R$ and $A\to A_0$ shows that $R$ and $A_0$ are Noetherian. Completion preserves Noetherianity, so $P$ is Noetherian; permanence applied to $P\to E=P/J$ shows that $E$ is Noetherian. Every ideal in these rings is therefore finitely generated. The completion-mod-ideal theorem applied to $(R,IR)$ shows that $P$ is $IP$-adically complete. Here powers of the extended ideals $IR,IP,IE$ are exactly the ideals generated by the corresponding powers of $I$.

Apply the finite-module completion comparison over the Noetherian ring $E$, with ideal $IE$ and cyclic module $E/HE$. Since $E$ is complete by hypothesis, its canonical comparison identifies $(E/HE)^\wedge_I$ with $E\otimes_E(E/HE)=E/HE$ and identifies the canonical completion map with the identity. Thus $E_0$ is $I$-adically complete. Apply the same comparison over $R$ with ideal $IR$ and cyclic module $R/HR$: it identifies $(R/HR)^\wedge_I$ with $P\otimes_R(R/HR)=P/HP$. The tensor-quotient identification sends $p\otimes\bar f$ to $p f\bmod HP$, with inverse $\bar p\mapsto p\otimes1$. The completion comparison sends this element to the compatible sequence of its reductions; it preserves products on pure tensors and hence on sums, so the identification is an algebra isomorphism. Finally $R/HR=R_0$ coefficientwise: a polynomial maps to zero exactly when its finitely many coefficients lie in $H$.

source.place: Tag 00MA (lemma-completion-tensor), part (3), with its canonical comparison map; the closed-quotient calculation is remark-take-bar in restricted.tex.

proof.text: Write $L=IA_0$. The equality $V(L)=V(K)$ implies $\sqrt L=\sqrt K$. Since $A_0$ is Noetherian, $L$ and $K$ are finitely generated. The finitely-generated radical-power lemma gives integers $u,v\geq1$ with $L^u\subseteq K$ and $K^v\subseteq L$. Extend these inclusions to $E_0$ and $R_0$. The change-of-ideal completion theorem shows that the $I$-complete ring $E_0$ is $K$-complete, and identifies $(R_0)^\wedge_I$ with $P_0=(R_0)^\wedge_K$. Together with Step 2 this gives a canonical coefficient-reduction surjection $\pi:P\to P_0$ with kernel $HP$. Put $J_0=\pi(J)=(J+HP)/HP$. Then $P_0/J_0=P/(J+HP)=E_0$ as $A_0$-algebras. This supplies the required presentation with $s=r$.

Let $M=J/J^2$ and $M_0=J_0/J_0^2$. The map $q:M\to M_0$, $[f]\mapsto[\pi(f)]$, is well defined and surjective: $\pi(J)=J_0$ and $\pi(J^2)=J_0^2$. It is $E$-linear for the action through $E\to E_0$, and $q(HM)=0$. Let $\rho:E^{\oplus r}\to E_0^{\oplus r}$ be coordinate reduction. Polynomial differentiation is $A$-linear and sends $I^nR$ into $I^nR$; it therefore acts on compatible sequences defining $P$. Reducing these sequences coefficientwise commutes with differentiation. The cofinal reindexing defining the change-of-ideal isomorphism in Step 3 also commutes with it, since $L^u\subseteq K$, $K^v\subseteq L$. Thus $\pi(\partial_i f)=\partial_i\pi(f)$ for every $f\in P$. The Leibniz rule gives $\partial_i(J^2)\subseteq J$ and $\partial_i(J_0^2)\subseteq J_0$. Consequently the induced continuous conormal differential $\delta_0:M_0\to E_0^{\oplus r}$ satisfies $\delta_0q=\rho\delta$.

source.place: A naive cotangent complex, equation-NL; elementary computation for remark-take-bar / equation-base-change-to-closed.

proof.text: Fix $a\in I^c$. Since $a\operatorname{coker}\delta=0$, choose $m_j\in M$ with $\delta(m_j)=a e_j$ for each of the $r$ standard basis vectors. Define the $E$-linear map $\alpha:E^{\oplus r}\to M$ by $\alpha(e_j)=m_j$; thus $\delta\alpha=a\operatorname{id}$. For every $m\in M$, $\delta(\alpha\delta(m)-am)=0$. Since $a\ker\delta=0$, we have $a\alpha\delta(m)=a^2m$. Therefore $h=a\alpha$ satisfies both $\delta h=a^2\operatorname{id}_{E^{\oplus r}}$ and $h\delta=a^2\operatorname{id}_M$. This is a basis lift and two direct compositions; no assertion that ordinary tensor product preserves kernels is used.

source.place: Elementary two-term calculation underlying lemma-equivalent-with-artin, equivalence of item-zero-on-cohomology-NL and item-zero-on-NL; written out here for the closed case.

proof.text: The map $qh:E^{\oplus r}\to M_0$ kills $H E^{\oplus r}$ by $E$-linearity, so it factors through a map $h_0:E_0^{\oplus r}\to M_0$ with $h_0\rho=qh$. The identities in Steps 4 and 5 give $\delta_0h_0\rho=\rho\delta h=\bar a^2\rho$ and $h_0\delta_0q=h_0\rho\delta=qh\delta=\bar a^2q$. Surjectivity of $\rho$ and $q$ gives $\delta_0h_0=\bar a^2\operatorname{id}$ and $h_0\delta_0=\bar a^2\operatorname{id}$. For $z\in\ker\delta_0$, $\bar a^2z=h_0\delta_0z=0$; for any class $[w]$ in the cokernel, $\bar a^2[w]=[\delta_0h_0w]=0$. Thus the image of $a^2$ annihilates both modules, for every $a\in I^c$.

source.place: Elementary closed-base-change computation refining lemma-zero-after-modding-out and lemma-base-change-rig-etale-homomorphism; it uses the explicit homotopies of Step 5.

proof.text: Choose generators $b_1,\ldots,b_t$ of the ideal $I^c$ in $A$; this is possible by the definition of Noetherianity. Each image $\bar b_i^2$ kills both modules by Step 6. Every product of $t+1$ generators $b_i$ has a repeated factor, so $(I^c)^{t+1}\subseteq(b_1^2,\ldots,b_t^2)$. If $t=0$, the left side is the zero ideal and this inclusion still holds. Hence $(IA_0)^{c(t+1)}$ annihilates both $\ker\delta_0$ and $\operatorname{coker}\delta_0$. With $v$ from Step 3, set $d=vc(t+1)\geq0$. Then $K^d=(K^v)^{c(t+1)}\subseteq(IA_0)^{c(t+1)}$, proving the required uniform annihilation. When $c=0$, the same formulas give $d=0$ and assert that both modules vanish; the homotopy identities already prove this. The presentation of Step 3 and its continuous differential of Step 4 finish all clauses.

The statement is 0GB2 for the closed map A→A/H, with rig-étale written as 0AJU(3). The base-change morphism is the source's own B/HB, as remark-take-bar identifies it. The hypotheses match: A Noetherian, V(IA_0)=V(K), E complete. Nothing is weakened. Step 1 (Noetherianity and completeness of P) and Step 2 (the finite-module tensor node over E and over R) give E/HE complete and P/HP≅(R_0)^∧_I. Step 3 (radical powers plus change of ideal) gives K-completeness and π:P↠P_0 with kernel HP, so the presentation exists with s=r. Step 4: q is well defined and surjective, ∂ commutes with reduction and with cofinal reindexing, and δ_0q=ρδ. Step 5: δh=hδ=a² with h=aα; I recomputed both. Step 6: the homotopy descends through the surjections q and ρ, with no flatness used. Step 7: pigeonhole gives (I^c)^{t+1}⊆(b_i²), so d=vc(t+1). I checked the edge cases r=0, H=0, H=A, I=0, I=A, c=0 and t=0. The parent (rig-etale-jacobian-algebraization, Step 4, H=(a^m)) uses the item consistently.
